proof_summary: Over \(\mathbf F_p\), Euler’s criterion, interpolation at the distinct squares \(1^2,\ldots,m^2\), signed-binomial finite-difference moments, and Wilson’s identity \((m!)^2=(-1)^{m+1}\) rule out a nonzero kernel when \(p\equiv1\pmod4\). When \(p\equiv3\pmod4\), writing \(\varepsilon\equiv m!=\pm1\), a quadratic-character sum makes the product with the partner matrix \((\chi(i^2+\varepsilon j))\) skew-symmetric of odd order, while the same interpolation-and-moment method proves the partner invertible, forcing the original determinant to vanish.
